program_name: Forward Capacity Market - Active Demand Capacity Resource (ADCR)
incentive_structure: $/kW-month Capacity Supply Obligation (CSO) payment = CSO kW x FCA clearing price; plus/minus Pay-for-Performance adjustments during Capacity Scarcity Conditions
incentive_value_usd: FCA 17 (CCP 2026/27): $2.590/kW-month all zones; FCA 18 (CCP 2027/28): $3.580/kW-month all zones (finalized); FCA 16 (CCP 2025/26) ~ $2.59/kW-month per IMM 2025 AMR
event_limits: ADCR maps to one or more Demand Response Resources (DRRs) in a single Dispatch Zone; each DRR >= 100 kW demand reduction; each Demand Response Asset (retail delivery point) >= 10 kW and must deliver 5-minute meter data in real time; seasonal audits (summer and winter) with reduction measured as baseline minus actual load at DRA level; must offer CSO into energy market and respond to ISO dispatch
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section III.13 (Forward Capacity Market); Market Rule 1 Section III.8B (Demand Response Baselines); Manual M-20 (Forward Capacity Market); Manual M-MVDR
export_compensation: No export compensation - demand reduction measured against customer baseline
stackable_with: Energy market (DRR offers required) + real-time reserves via same DRR; FCA 18 is the last Forward Capacity Auction - FCA 19 replaced by prompt auction (see CAR-PD row)

program_name: Forward Capacity Market - FCA 18 clearing price (Capacity Commitment Period 2027/2028)
incentive_structure: $/kW-month uniform clearing price
incentive_value_usd: $3.580/kW-month all zones and import interfaces (finalized; CCP Jun 1 2027 - May 31 2028); 2,614 MW of new and existing demand resources cleared
event_limits: Auction held Feb 5 2024; FCA 18 is the final forward (3-year-ahead) auction before the transition to the prompt capacity auction
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section III.13.2; Manual M-20

program_name: Forward Capacity Market - FCA 17 clearing price (Capacity Commitment Period 2026/2027)
incentive_structure: $/kW-month uniform clearing price
incentive_value_usd: $2.590/kW-month all zones and import interfaces except New Brunswick interface ($2.551/kW-month) (preliminary per press release; CCP Jun 1 2026 - May 31 2027); 2,940 MW of demand resources cleared incl. 130 MW new
event_limits: Auction closed Mar 6 2023
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section III.13.2; Manual M-20

program_name: Pay-for-Performance - Capacity Performance Payment Rate (PPR)
incentive_structure: $/MWh charge or credit during Capacity Scarcity Conditions: Capacity Performance Payment = PPR x (Actual Capacity Provided - Balancing Ratio x CSO) per 5-minute interval; Balancing Ratio = (Load + Reserve Requirement) / total system CSO, capped at 1.0 per FERC order EL25-106
event_limits: Applies to every CSO holder (incl. ADCRs and DERAs with CSO) and also credits non-CSO resources that over-perform during a scarcity condition; FERC Jan 22 2026 order in EL25-106 capped the Balancing Ratio at 1.0 (compliance filing due Jul 21 2026, refund effective date Jul 25 2025); ISO proposed allocating deficient funds to over-performers (effective PPR for over-performance can fall below $9,337/MWh) and removing Capacity Performance Bilaterals
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section III.13.7 (Performance, Payments and Charges in the FCM)
stackable_with: Paid on top of FCM base payment and energy/reserve revenue

program_name: Capacity Auction Reforms - Prompt/Deactivation (CAR-PD) replacing FCA 19
incentive_structure: $/kW-month prompt capacity auction held shortly before the Capacity Commitment Period (instead of ~3 years ahead)
event_limits: FCA 19 (originally for CCP 2028/29) was delayed under FERC acceptance of ISO's further-delay filing (ER24-1710-000); CAR-PD accepted by FERC Mar 30 2026 (ER26-925-000); first prompt auction held in 2028 for CCP beginning Jun 1 2028; retirement decisions decoupled from auction via new deactivation notice process
tariff_schedule: FERC Dockets ER24-1710-000 and ER26-925-000; Tariff Section III.13 (as revised)

program_name: Capacity Auction Reforms - Seasonal/Accreditation (CAR-SA)
incentive_structure: Seasonal (summer/winter) $/kW-month capacity commitments with updated capacity accreditation
event_limits: Moves the Capacity Commitment Period from annual to sub-annual (seasonal) structure and updates capacity accreditation; intended for CCP starting Jun 1 2028; FERC filing expected Q4 2026 - not yet filed/approved as of last_verified
tariff_schedule: ISO-NE CAR-SA proposal (NEPOOL MC/RC/TC Sep 8-10 2026 design update)

program_name: FERC Order 2222 - DER Aggregation (DERA) participation models - energy and ancillary services
incentive_structure: $/MWh LMP for energy and ancillary-service clearing prices, settled at LD pnode or DRR aggregation zone pnode depending on model
event_limits: Effective Nov 1 2026. Minimum aggregation size 100 kW; any single resource or aggregation >= 5 MW at a single node must participate standalone or via a more geographically limited aggregation. Seven models: SODERA (settlement-only generator and/or load asset, new Day-Ahead Market asset types); DRDERA (SOG + DRR assets, may include load, activation/deactivation on monthly boundary); Modeled Generator asset (fuel index 'DER aggregation'); Binary Storage Facility; Continuous Storage Facility; DRR; ATRR (regulation, min 0.1 MW, >=5 MW restricted to node)
tariff_schedule: FERC Order No. 2222; ISO-NE compliance filings ER22-983; Market Rule 1 (as revised effective Nov 1 2026)
export_compensation: Injections settled at LMP under SODERA/DDERA models
stackable_with: Capacity participation for DERAs (Distributed Energy Capacity Resource) starts later - see capacity row

program_name: Energy market price levels - 2025 average Day-Ahead and Real-Time LMP (IMM Annual Markets Report)
incentive_structure: $/MWh LMP (reference value for energy arbitrage / DRR energy payments)
incentive_value_usd: 2025 average Day-Ahead LMP $71.81/MWh (+73% vs 2024); 2025 average Real-Time LMP $65.89/MWh (+67% vs 2024); avg natural gas $6.27/MMBtu (2024: $3.06)
event_limits: Region-wide annual averages as reported by the IMM; nodal and zonal values differ
tariff_schedule: ISO-NE Internal Market Monitor 2025 Annual Markets Report

program_name: Demand Response Resource (DRR) - Day-Ahead and Real-Time Energy Market participation (Price-Responsive Demand)
incentive_structure: $/MWh: demand reduction (MWh) paid at Real-Time LMP for each 5-minute interval of the dispatch period, as if generated; Day-Ahead cleared reductions settled at Day-Ahead LMP
incentive_value_usd: Reference: 2023 average Real-Time LMP $35.70/MWh; 88% of DRRs offered at $1,000/MWh in 2023 (per ISO)
event_limits: DRA (retail customer site) >= 10 kW reduction capability with near-real-time meter data; DRR = one or more DRAs collectively >= 100 kW; a DRA >= 5 MW must be its own DRR; DRRs submit DA and RT offers, can be committed day-ahead and dispatched in real time, are co-optimized for energy and reserves and can set price; dispatched when RT price >= offer price, usually a few hours around the evening peak. Baseline: DRA average use over the last 10 weekdays, adjusted by the DRA's average use in the 15 minutes before the start-up instruction; reduction = adjusted baseline minus actual use; offers subject to the Demand Reduction Threshold Price floor (see separate row)
tariff_schedule: Market Rule 1 Section III.8B (Demand Response Baselines); Section III.1.10.1A (DRR offers); Manual M-MVDR; Price-Responsive Demand framework effective Jun 1 2018
export_compensation: No export compensation for DRR model - payment is for reduction vs baseline (battery discharge behind the RDP reduces metered load)
stackable_with: Real-time reserves and DA ancillary services via same DRR; capacity via Active Demand Capacity Resource (ADCR) mapping; utility retail DR (e.g. ConnectedSolutions) is outside ISO dispatch - dual-participation rules not stated on source

program_name: Demand Reduction Threshold Price - Order 745 net-benefits offer floor for Demand Response Resources
incentive_structure: Minimum $/MWh offer price for DRR demand reductions, calculated monthly from the reference-month supply curve (Order 745 net benefits test)
event_limits: Calculated per Market Rule 1 Section III.1.10.1A(f); published monthly by ISO in the Demand-Response Threshold Price Summary/Details reports (ISO Express) - monthly $/MWh values not retrieved
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section I.2.2 (definition of Demand Reduction Threshold Price); Market Rule 1 Section III.1.10.1A(f) and III.1.10.1A(e)(ii)
stackable_with: Applies to all DRR energy offers

program_name: Passive Demand Capacity Resources - On-Peak Demand Resource
incentive_structure: $/kW-month Forward Capacity Market CSO payment for measured load reduction during fixed on-peak hours (capacity market only)
incentive_value_usd: Paid FCA clearing price - see FCA 17/18 rows ($2.590 and $3.580/kW-month)
event_limits: Non-dispatchable; capacity market only - ineligible for energy/reserve markets. Performance hours: summer non-holiday weekdays 1-5 pm Jun-Aug; winter non-holiday weekdays 5-7 pm Dec-Jan. Examples: energy efficiency, passive behind-the-meter solar
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section III.13 (FCM); Manual M-MVDR (Measurement and Verification of Demand Reduction Value)
on_peak_window: Summer: non-holiday weekdays 1-5pm Jun-Aug; Winter: non-holiday weekdays 5-7pm Dec-Jan

program_name: Passive Demand Capacity Resources - Seasonal Peak Demand Resource
incentive_structure: $/kW-month Forward Capacity Market CSO payment for measured load reduction during system-peak hours (capacity market only)
incentive_value_usd: Paid FCA clearing price - see FCA 17/18 rows
event_limits: Non-dispatchable; capacity market only. Performance hours: non-holiday weekdays in Jun-Aug and Dec-Jan when real-time system hourly load >= 90% of the most recent 50/50 CELT seasonal peak-load forecast
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section III.13 (FCM); Manual M-MVDR
on_peak_window: Non-holiday weekdays Jun-Aug and Dec-Jan in hours with RT system load >= 90% of 50/50 seasonal peak forecast

program_name: FERC Order 2222 - Distributed Energy Capacity Resource (DECR) capacity market participation - effective date
incentive_structure: $/kW-month capacity payment for DER Aggregations qualified as Distributed Energy Capacity Resources
event_limits: Gate: Tariff changes affecting Forward Capacity Market rules are effective for the 2028-29 Capacity Commitment Period (CCP 19); originally targeted FCA 18, pushed to FCA 19 after FERC's Mar 1 2023 order; FCA 19 then delayed and replaced by prompt auction (CAR-PD) - additional CCP 19 changes reflecting capacity auction reforms expected to be filed ahead of CCP 19. FCM Order 2222 software (qualification of DECRs) completed Feb 2024 (search snippet, not verified on page). Energy/ancillary rules separately effective Nov 1 2026
tariff_schedule: FERC Order No. 2222; ER22-983; Tariff Section III.13 (as revised for CCP 19)
stackable_with: See Order 2222 energy/AS DERA row and CAR-PD row

program_name: FERC Order 2222 - behind-the-meter DER metering and eligibility restrictions for DER Aggregations (net-metered / retail program exclusion)
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate (no payment)
event_limits: Meters of behind-the-meter DERs must be located at the Retail Delivery Point (RDP); DER sub-metering allowed only if the Host Utility can accommodate metering configurations that address double-counting; metering must comply with OP-18 and Manual M-28. DER Aggregator is responsible for meter data (FERC 185 FERC 61,021, Oct 6 2023 sustained this; ISO final compliance filing Jan 31 2024) and may designate itself, an agent, or the Host Participant as Assigned Meter Reader. Distribution utility has 60 calendar days to confirm each DER: net consumption/injection not included in another Load Asset; NOT participating in a retail program that prohibits wholesale market participation; safety/reliability; interconnection agreement executed where state rules require. Distribution utility may override ISO dispatch of a DERA for distribution safety/reliability. FERC Mar 1 2023 order (182 FERC 61,137) had found RDP-metering proposal inadequately supported - final accepted status of RDP rule taken from ISO 2025/2026 presentations
tariff_schedule: FERC Docket ER22-983 (182 FERC 61,137; 185 FERC 61,021; 187 FERC 61,100); ISO OP-18; Manual M-28
export_compensation: Net-metered BTM DERs: participation depends on retail program terms - utility confirms DER is not in a retail program prohibiting wholesale participation
stackable_with: Cannot be counted in another Load Asset; retail program stacking governed by state/utility rules

program_name: FERC Order 2222 - small distribution utility opt-in (<= 4 million MWh annual)
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate (no payment)
event_limits: ISO-NE compliance implements the Order 2222 opt-in provision for distribution companies with <= 4 million MWh of annual deliveries/sales: under Order 2222 the RTO may not accept DERs from such utilities into aggregations unless the relevant electric retail regulatory authority permits (opt-in). Which New England small utilities or RERRAs have opted in was not found
tariff_schedule: FERC Order No. 2222 (directive 11); ER22-983

program_name: Distributed Energy Resource equivalent Capacity Network Resource Capability (CNRC) - deliverability pathway for DERs
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate for capacity market (no payment)
event_limits: Accepted by FERC May 29 2026 (ER26-1956-000, 195 FERC 61,156), effective May 29 2026. DERs (incl. Distributed Energy Capacity Resources and Active Demand Capacity Resources) in areas found deliverable in the latest cluster-study deliverability analysis may establish equivalent CNRC by (1) clearing a Capacity Supply Obligation (first cleared, first served) or (2) 'lock-in' request with state interconnection agreement, proof of commercial readiness, and COD <= 2.5 years out. Equivalent NRC for DER generating facilities from state interconnection agreement values (not DRRs/DERAs)
tariff_schedule: Tariff Section II.48 (II.48.5.1-II.48.5.3); FERC Docket ER26-1956-000

program_name: Day-Ahead Ancillary Services Market - Flexible Response Services (DA TMSR / DA TMNSR / DA TMOR)
incentive_structure: $/MWh day-ahead clearing price per hourly award (call option): credit = award MW x clearing price; closeout charge = award MW x max(RT Hub LMP - Strike Price, 0); Strike Price = expected RT Hub LMP + $10/MWh
incentive_value_usd: First-year (Mar 2025-Feb 2026) net settlements: DA TMSR $74.4M, DA TMNSR $113.6M, DA TMOR $60.3M; FRS clearing prices averaged $16-17/MWh Summer 2025 and $12-13/MWh Fall 2025; DA TMOR monthly averages $5.43/MWh Sep 2025, $12.20/MWh Oct 2025, $19.25/MWh Nov 2025; clearing prices cascade TMSR >= TMNSR >= TMOR; fleetwide DA A/S revenue ~ $3.50/kW-month (vs ~$1.30/kW-month under former Forward Reserve Market 2023-24)
event_limits: Live for operating day Mar 1 2025 (replaced Forward Reserve Market); voluntary; generators, Demand Response Resources and Dispatchable Asset Related Demand must submit hourly price-quantity A/S offers in the Day-Ahead Market; optional Maximum Daily Award Limit (MDAL). Requirements: Total 10 = first contingency x non-performance factor (115% since May 1 2026, was 120%); TMSR generally 25% of Total 10; Total 30 adds 50% of second contingency + 160-180 MW replacement reserves. First-year clearing dominated by oil/gas CTs and gas CCs; batteries not separately reported
tariff_schedule: Market Rule 1 Section III.1.7.19.2 (reserve capability); ISO Operating Procedure OP-8; Day-Ahead Ancillary Services Initiative (DASI)
stackable_with: Co-optimized with Day-Ahead Energy; award carries real-time closeout exposure; DRDERAs added to DA A/S from Nov 1 2026 (Order 2222 conforming changes)

program_name: Day-Ahead Ancillary Services Market - Energy Imbalance Reserve (EIR) and Forecast Energy Requirement Price (FERP)
incentive_structure: $/MWh: cleared EIR paid FERP only; cleared day-ahead energy from physical supply (generators, DRRs, imports) paid LMP + FERP; EIR subject to same call-option closeout
incentive_value_usd: First-year (Mar 2025-Feb 2026) EIR net settlements $13.4M; FER credits ~ $1,005M ($8.49/MWh of load); average annual FER price $7.13/MWh (all hours incl. zero-price hours)
event_limits: 60-minute reserve capability used to meet the Forecast Energy Requirement (ISO next-day load forecast) together with day-ahead physical energy awards
tariff_schedule: Market Rule 1 (DASI provisions); Day-Ahead Ancillary Services Initiative
stackable_with: Co-optimized with Day-Ahead Energy and FRS

program_name: Day-Ahead Ancillary Services Market - 2026 post-implementation changes (non-performance factor, strike price floor, FER adjustment)
incentive_structure: Parameter changes affecting DA A/S clearing prices and closeout exposure
incentive_value_usd: ISO estimated savings ~ $23M/yr (per trade press); IMM estimated first-year incremental DA A/S cost $974M
event_limits: Non-performance factor cut from 120% to 115% effective operating day May 1 2026 (lowers TMSR and total reserve requirements) - verified on ISO page. Strike price floor and downward FER Demand Quantity adjustment (IMM recommendation Feb 4 2026): trade press reports FERC accepted the ISO/NEPOOL filing Sep 14 2026 in Docket ER26-3176-000, adjusting four DA A/S parameters, effective Oct 22 2026 - not verified on an ISO or FERC page; ISO readiness page (updated Aug 13 2026) still lists implementation date TBA
tariff_schedule: FERC Docket ER26-3176-000 (reported); ISO OP-8

program_name: Real-Time Operating Reserves (TMSR / TMNSR / TMOR) - real-time reserve pricing
incentive_structure: $/MWh real-time reserve clearing price paid on designated reserve MW in 5-minute intervals; non-zero only when ISO must re-dispatch to hold reserves
incentive_value_usd: Fall 2025 average non-zero prices: TMSR $22.63/MWh (133.4 hours priced; $13.82/MWh excl. Nov 23 2025 scarcity day), TMNSR $200.38/MWh (9.8 h), TMOR $151.86/MWh (9.7 h); Fall 2024: TMSR $6.39 (196.1 h), TMNSR $15.06 (0.3 h), TMOR $0.00 (0 h)
event_limits: Demand Response Resources are co-optimized for energy and reserves in real time (Price-Responsive Demand framework, Jun 1 2018). During the Nov 23 2025 capacity scarcity condition the 30-minute reserve price hit $1,000/MWh (30-min RCPF) and total 10-minute reserve price $2,500/MWh (30-min price + $1,000 10-min RCPF); oil, hydro and battery storage units ramping up created ten-minute spinning reserves. Four intervals in Fall 2025 had a binding TMNSR RCPF ($1,500/MWh above TMOR)
tariff_schedule: Market Rule 1 (real-time reserve pricing - section number not verified); ISO Operating Procedure OP-8
stackable_with: Energy market (co-optimized); DA A/S awards; capacity (Pay-for-Performance)

program_name: Regulation Market - Alternative Technology Regulation Resource (ATRR) and generator regulation
incentive_structure: Two clearing prices: $/MW-hr regulation capacity price and $/MW service (mileage) price; paid on cleared regulation capacity and mileage
incentive_value_usd: Fall 2025 total regulation payments $4.02M (Fall 2024 $4.3M); capacity prices down 21% year over year; Fall 2025 average cleared regulation 110 MW of which ATRRs 92 MW (84%); ATRR available capacity 598 MW (Fall 2024: 237 MW); IMM 2025 AMR: battery net revenue just under $10/kW-month in 2025, down on lower regulation prices; regulation RSI > 900% (large excess supply). Average $/MW-hr capacity and mileage prices not captured
event_limits: ATRR: one or more facilities providing regulation (almost all batteries in New England); current rule: ATRR with >= 1 MW regulation capacity registers as a separate ATRR (Tariff Section I.2.2 definition, via search snippet); under Order 2222 compliance the ATRR minimum drops from 1 MW to 100 kW with a locational requirement and the generator minimum size for regulation is reduced, effective Nov 1 2026 (ISO Order 2222 refresher). Batteries may participate as regulation-only ATRRs or combine charging, discharging and regulation
tariff_schedule: Market Rule 1 Section III.14 (Regulation Market); ISO Operating Procedure OP-14 / OP-8
stackable_with: Batteries may combine regulation with energy (charge/discharge) participation; regulation MW reduce capability available for reserves

program_name: State / RERRA opt-out of third-party demand response aggregation (FERC Order 719 prohibition notice)
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate (no payment)
event_limits: Host utility submits the ISO form 'Notification of Service Territory Position on Demand Response Registration' stating whether its relevant electric retail regulatory authority prohibits or permits registration of its customers' demand response by aggregators; FERC rules bar ISO from accepting aggregator bids where the RERRA prohibits it. No New England state or utility prohibition was found, but the per-utility notification data is not published on the page - state positions unverified
tariff_schedule: FERC Order 719 (18 CFR 35.28(g)(1)); ISO-NE demand response registration form
